issue_context.title: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy CEL validation rules do not seem to expand `__dot__` and `__slash__` as written in the documentation
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

Given the rule:
```
"!has(object.metadata.labels) || (has(object.metadata.labels) && !object.metadata.labels.helm__dot__sh__slash__chart == 'other')"
```
does not seem to expand the \_\_dot\_\_ and \_\_slash\_\_ because it gives the error 
```
Error from server (Invalid): error when creating "manifests/test.yaml": secrets "test" is forbidden: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy 'block-helm-other' with binding 'block-helm-other' denied request: expression '!has(object.metadata.labels) || (has(object.metadata.labels) && object.metadata.labels.helm__dot__sh__chart__chart == 'other')' resulted in error: no such key: helm__dot__sh__chart__chart
```
And of course just guarding it with another has() macro doesn't work since that will just return false.

You end up with
```
!has(object.metadata.labels) || (has(object.metadata.labels) && !has(object.metadata.labels.helm__dot__sh__chart__chart)) || (has(object.metadata.labels) && !has(object.metadata.labels.helm__dot__sh__slash__chart) && !object.metadata.labels.helm__dot__sh__slash__chart.startsWith('other'))
```
for example but that lets everything pass because `!has(object.metadata.labels.helm__dot__sh__slash__chart)` is returns true.

### What did you expect to happen?

This should block anything with the label like this:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: "test"
  labels:
    helm.sh/chart: other
```

instead it doesn't stop this at all.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

The policies
```yaml
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
metadata:
  name: "block-helm-other"
spec:
  failurePolicy: Fail
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups:   ["*"]
      apiVersions: ["*"]
      operations:  ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
      resources:   ["*"]
  validations:
    - expression: "!has(object.metadata.labels) || (has(object.metadata.labels) && object.metadata.labels.helm__dot__sh__slash___chart == 'other')"
---
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding
metadata:
  name: "block-helm-other"
spec:
  policyName: "block-helm-other"
  validationActions: [Deny]
```

and then try this secret:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: "test"
  labels:
    helm.sh/chart: other
data:
  test: ""
```

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

comments: If this ends up needing a change to docs, please either transfer it (Prow command `/transfer website`) or open a new linked issue, whichever feels more appropriate.
I feel like this is a worthy feature, so instead of removing the docs, fixing it would be better. Otherwise checking on most labels would be impossible (given they often contains dots and slashes).
We document some bugs, even if a later patch release fixes them. This might be one of 'em.

> feel like this is a worthy feature, so instead of removing the docs, fixing it would be better. Otherwise checking on most labels would be impossible (given they often contains dots and slashes).

can you access labels using ["..."] notation?
/retitle ValidatingAdmissionPolicy CEL validation rules do not seem to expand `__dot__` and `__slash__` as written in the documentation

> can you access labels using ["..."] notation?

This seems to break the usage of the `has()` macro.

```yaml
validations:
    - expression: |
        !has(object.metadata.labels["helm.sh/chart"])
```
leads to

```
The ValidatingAdmissionPolicy "block-calcasa-helm" is invalid: spec.validations[0].expression: Invalid value: "!has(object.metadata.labels[\"helm.sh/chart\"])\n": compilation failed: ERROR: <input>:1:5: invalid argument to has() macro
 | !has(object.metadata.labels["helm.sh/chart"])
 | ....^
```

Just accessing like this:

```yaml
- expression: |
    object.metadata.labels["helm.sh/chart"] != "other"
```

Does work, but I kind of need a rule that guards against the label not existing, otherwise the rule blocks other items like this:

```
secrets "test" is forbidden: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy 'block-helm-other' with binding 'block-helm-other' denied request: expression 'object.metadata.labels["helm.sh/chart"] != "other"
' resulted in error: no such key: helm.sh/chart
```

In CEL, `has()` is for fields, and `in` is for map keys. Try:

```
"helm.sh/chart" in object.metadata.labels
```

> In CEL, `has()` is for fields, and `in` is for map keys. Try:
> 
> ```
> "helm.sh/chart" in object.metadata.labels
> ```

Thanks this does indeed work. Though the documentation is not super clear in my opinion, it's fixed for me now.
Resulting in this condition:

```
!has(object.metadata.labels) || (has(object.metadata.labels) && !("helm.sh/chart" in object.metadata.labels)) || (has(object.metadata.labels) && "helm.sh/chart" in object.metadata.labels && !object.metadata.labels["helm.sh/chart"].startsWith('other'))
```

Though this seems awfully complicated to just bar some value in a label. And it has essentially 2 ways to write the same thing, and it requires knowing labels is a map. It would be great if `has()` could also work, and if the substitutions like `__dot__` just worked every time and everywhere.

Some operator like `?.` from C# would be awesome. So we could write
```
!object.metadata?.labels?.helm__dot__sh__slash__chart?.startsWith('other')
```

To ignore any non existent items would be great. `?.` will just return null and stop the evaluation when the object in front of is, is null/does not exist. Although maybe I have just missed some higher CEL technique of course. Having some documentation on this from some of the experts would be awesome. Especially since k8s has quite some maps with dots and slashes in the keys (labels and annotations come to mind).

@EraYaN, if you can suggest what isn't clear in a new [documentation issue](https://github.com/kubernetes/website/issues/new/choose) then that might help us explain things better when this moves from alpha to beta.

Please do consider filing that issue.
(we won't be able to consider enhancements to CEL; we document Kubernetes as it is, not as folk might like it to be)

@sftim Alright I have created a documentation issue as well, hopefully I did a good enough job of articulating my struggles, maybe it needs to be split up, but I'm not sure, so I kept it to one for the time being.

> Some operator like `?.` from C# would be awesome. So we could write
> 
> ```
> !object.metadata?.labels?.helm__dot__sh__slash__chart?.startsWith('other')
> ```

I completely agree. We're merging support for `.?` via https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118339.

See https://github.com/google/cel-spec/wiki/proposal-246 for exact grammar.
